## Evaluation of the Justification for Israel's 2008-2009 Military Operations Against Gaza

### Background and Context
The 2008-2009 military operations, known as Operation Cast Lead, were conducted by Israel in the Gaza Strip. The operations were launched in response to ongoing rocket attacks by Hamas and other militant groups targeting Israeli civilians. The operations aimed to stop these attacks and restore Israel's deterrence power.

### Justification of the Operations
The justification for Israel's military operations is rooted in the right to self-defense under international law. Prior to the operations, Hamas had launched thousands of rockets into Israel, killing and injuring numerous civilians. Israel's response was seen as a legitimate measure to protect its citizens. According to then-President-elect Barack Obama, "If somebody was sending rockets into my house where my two daughters sleep at night, I would do everything to stop that, and would expect Israel to do the same thing." [1]

### Civilian Casualties and Proportionality
Despite the justification for the operations, the issue of civilian casualties and the proportionality of the response has been a significant point of contention. Israel's military operations were designed to minimize civilian casualties, with precision strikes targeting military sites. Benjamin Netanyahu argued that Israel's actions were proportionate and aimed at minimizing civilian deaths. [3] However, the high number of civilian casualties in Gaza has led to criticism that the operations were disproportionate and excessive.

### Excesses and Criticisms
Critics argue that the operations went beyond what was necessary for self-defense and resulted in significant civilian harm. The operations were seen by some as an overreaction, given the context of the ongoing conflict and the historical grievances of both sides. The Foreign Minister of Israel, Avigdor Lieberman, stated that a return to the 1967 borders would make Israel vulnerable to future attacks, thus justifying a strong response to deter future aggression. [4]

### Conclusion
The justification for Israel's 2008-2009 military operations against Gaza is complex and multifaceted. While the operations were seen as a legitimate response to ongoing rocket attacks and a necessary measure to protect Israeli civilians, the high number of civilian casualties in Gaza has led to significant criticism. The operations were justified under the principle of self-defense, but the proportionality and necessity of the response remain contentious issues.

FULL EVIDENCE PASSAGE:
Operation Cast Lead was justified as it was proportionate to Hamas' rocket attacks against Israel. It should be remembered that 250,000 Israelis living in the southern part of the country had lived under years of terrorism before Operation Cast Lead was launched, often in bomb shelters, and the economy has suffered. The world's media may only have paid attention when Israel responded to Hamas' barrage, but this does not mean that Israel was not already under severe attack by this point. But according to internationally accepted laws of war, Israel is permitted to respond with the force necessary to end the conflict. Provoked by Hamas, Israel had every right to wage a disproportionate and overwhelming response. Hamas has repeatedly stated that its objective is to destroy Israel. Such an existential threat goes beyond simply Hamas' rocket attacks, as it portends much more destructive attacks in the future. This justifies defensive attacks from Israel that go beyond responding merely to the Hamas rockets, and would even justify Israeli efforts to fully demobilize or destroy Hamas. Israeli precision strikes sought to minimize civilian deaths, as Benjamin Netanyahu argued: "In launching precision strikes against Hamas rocket launchers, headquarters, weapons depots, smuggling tunnels and training camps, Israel is trying to minimize civilian casualties. "(13) Unlike Hamas, Israeli strikes targeted military sites, not civilians. As Gary Grant argued: "Even if you target your action at military sites, civilians are inevitably going to get killed...these need to be contrasted with the actions of Hamas where every single rocket is designed to attack civilian populations, so every single act of Hamas in firing these rockets is clearly an illegal act without any legal justification. "(2) Israel may have been justified in acting disproportionately, but instead chose to respond in a proportionate and limited manner which minimized civilian deaths in Gaza, and thus the Israeli military operations were certainly justified.

"(1) Prior to Israel's 2008-2009 military operations, Hamas had consistently violated the terms of the ceasefire between Gaza and Israel. It launched a total 6,300 rockets during an agreed hiatus in the confrontation, killing 10 and wounding more than 780. Hamas refused to extend the truce past 19 December 2008 and subsequently resumed attacks, firing nearly 300 more missiles, rockets and mortars. Just a few days before Israel's military operations, outgoing Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert made an appeal on the Arab television station Al-Arabiya asking Gaza residents to stop the firing of rockets and mortar shells so that a military response could be avoided. Gaza was also a test case, intended to prove that Israel remained a legitimate and authoritative actor in the region. Much more was at stake than merely the military outcome of Israel's operation. The issue, rather, was Israel's ability to restore its deterrence power and uphold the principle that its citizens cannot be targeted with impunity. "(5) Therefore there can be no debate that Israel had the right to defend itself as well as the right to determine how best to do so. While it is easy for countries and foreigners to state their opinions about Israel's security interests and how its actions may or may not fulfill them, Israel's right to make that judgment itself must be respected. Therefore Israel's military operations against Gaza were justified as legitimate self defense against Hamas and militant aggression which was putting the lives of Israeli citizens in jeopardy.

FULL EVIDENCE PASSAGE:
Operation Cast Lead was justified as it was proportionate to Hamas' rocket attacks against Israel. It should be remembered that 250,000 Israelis living in the southern part of the country had lived under years of terrorism before Operation Cast Lead was launched, often in bomb shelters, and the economy has suffered. The world's media may only have paid attention when Israel responded to Hamas' barrage, but this does not mean that Israel was not already under severe attack by this point. But according to internationally accepted laws of war, Israel is permitted to respond with the force necessary to end the conflict. Provoked by Hamas, Israel had every right to wage a disproportionate and overwhelming response. Hamas has repeatedly stated that its objective is to destroy Israel. Such an existential threat goes beyond simply Hamas' rocket attacks, as it portends much more destructive attacks in the future. This justifies defensive attacks from Israel that go beyond responding merely to the Hamas rockets, and would even justify Israeli efforts to fully demobilize or destroy Hamas. Israeli precision strikes sought to minimize civilian deaths, as Benjamin Netanyahu argued: "In launching precision strikes against Hamas rocket launchers, headquarters, weapons depots, smuggling tunnels and training camps, Israel is trying to minimize civilian casualties. "(13) Unlike Hamas, Israeli strikes targeted military sites, not civilians. As Gary Grant argued: "Even if you target your action at military sites, civilians are inevitably going to get killed...these need to be contrasted with the actions of Hamas where every single rocket is designed to attack civilian populations, so every single act of Hamas in firing these rockets is clearly an illegal act without any legal justification. "(2) Israel may have been justified in acting disproportionately, but instead chose to respond in a proportionate and limited manner which minimized civilian deaths in Gaza, and thus the Israeli military operations were certainly justified.

   - Operation Cast Lead was justified as it was proportionate to Hamas' rocket attacks against Israel. 250,000 Israelis in the southern part of the country had lived under years of terrorism before the operation, often in bomb shelters, and the economy had suffered.
